subject: Re: Neptune Analytics — request for custom SLA & runbook
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <agomez@neptune-analytics.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Neptune request: SLA & on-call runbook for strategic deployment

Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Neptune's execs are keen to move forward but they have one gating item: a written uptime/latency commitment and an on-call runbook for their inference production. Their basic asks are below: 

- Availability: 99.95% monthly uptime or better
- Latency: p95 < 80ms for inference (90 token prompts) — ideal but they indicated some flexibility
- Maintenance: pre-approved maintenance windows only, advance notice, guaranteed rollback timeline
- Operational artifacts: runbook, escalation contacts, and post-incident credit policy

I've attached a draft SLA they sent (Neptune_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf). Procurement wants to see a Redwood-approved response before DocuSign.

Can Redwood confirm whether the latency + availability target is feasible for their workload? If not, what would a production-ready counterproposal look like (dedicated capacity / pricing / runbook)?

Priya Shah (cc) will own procurement on their side; she needs a MAP and estimated delta in monthly cost before their legal signs off.

Appreciate a quick thumbs up / or a plan to review early next week.

Thanks,
Alex
Account Lead — Neptune Analytics

Attachment: Neptune_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc:
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700

Team — forwarding Neptune's request. This is a strategic account with expansion potential; they asked for 99.95% and p95 < 80ms. Key asks below and what I need from each of you: 

- Marissa: commercial stance — is 99.95 + p95 80ms something we can price and push for? Any precedent?
- Marcus: ops/infra feasibility — what changes would be required (dedicated pool, standby capacity, changes to batching/quant)? High-level cost delta please (ballpark is fine).
- Laura: legal — any standard carveouts we should include for maintenance/force majeure?

Plan: I'd like a short internal decision doc by EOD tomorrow so I can share a counterproposal with Alex on Monday. If feasible, we'll propose a 4-week pilot on dedicated capacity and a 12-month commitment with credits tied to monthly uptime.

I've attached a simple cost template — please populate rough numbers and call out unknowns: cost-impact-estimate.xlsx

Thanks — Karthik
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Quick technical readout — high level feasibility and constraints: 

Summary: Neptune's target is aggressive for a multi-tenant setup at scale. To reliably meet p95 < 80ms at realistic QPS we should plan for dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) + the following ops commitments: 

- Dedicated pool sizing: estimate for their expected peak QPS (Alex, please ask for QPS by model and concurrency). We'll need a baseline (I'll use their demo numbers for an initial calc).
- Standby capacity: warm standby nodes (20-30%) to meet sudden spikes without cold starts.
- Isolation: restrict noisy-neighbor batching on that pool; continuous batching disabled for critical routes.
- Quantization/Model variant: favored path is a quantized model with validated quality regression tests (we may need an eval run).
- Maintenance windows: agree to 2 scheduled windows per month, avoid high-traffic hours; emergency maintenance with rollback guarantee within 60 minutes.
- Telemetry / SLIs: token-level latency histograms, p95/p99, error-rate, and KV cache hit ratio to verify system health.
- Runbook: attach initial stub (runbook-stub.txt) that describes escalation steps, primary/secondary on-call, and rollback playbook.

If the customer signs for dedicated capacity, achieving p95 ~70-90ms looks possible depending on model and payload size. For multi-tenant we would recommend a staged SLO: p95 120ms shared, p95 80ms for dedicated. I put preliminary numbers in the cost sheet — see cost-impact-estimate.xlsx (tab: Neptune_calc).

Open items I need from product/ML infra team: guidance on best-practice kernel selection and any known limits for 90-token inference at their projected concurrency.

-- Marcus
Head of Platform Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachment: runbook-stub.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Neptune request: SLA & on-call runbook for strategic deployment

Karthik / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick analysis. Commercial thoughts: 

- We can include a 99.95% uptime commitment for a 12-month committed plan if Neptune accepts dedicated capacity pricing + a small premium for standby capacity.
- Offer a staged latency guarantee in the agreement:
  * Pilot period (4 weeks): measure stability and tune — no latency credit during pilot
  * Post-pilot (production): p95 <= 90ms for dedicated pool; with an option to step to 80ms if Neptune agrees to model/quantization constraints and additional validation testing.
- Credit policy: we should propose a monthly credit schedule (e.g., prorated credit up to a cap) tied to measurable SLIs. Legal will draft language.

Ask Karthik: propose MAP for Neptune that includes: pilot scope, trial acceptance criteria, dedicated capacity estimate, pricing delta, and timeline to decision. Once we have that, loop in Laura for legal redline and I'd like an exec-level review if they push for 80ms as a hard requirement.

I'll own pricing conversation and initial concession structure. Marcus — can you confirm the rollback / emergency maintenance SLA (the 60-minute rollback commitment you mentioned) as an OK internal expectation? If that's conservative enough, we'll include it.

-Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Alex / Priya — thanks for the note and for the draft SLA. Internal team has reviewed and here's a proposed path forward: 

1) Pilot (4 weeks) on dedicated reserved capacity
   - Purpose: validate p95 latency and operational behaviors at Neptune's expected QPS
   - Commitment: Redwood will provision a dedicated GPU pool with warm standby (20% buffer) for the pilot
   - Telemetry: we'll stream p95/p99, error rate, and cache metrics to a shared dashboard

2) Post-pilot production terms
   - Availability: offer 99.95% monthly uptime for the dedicated pool (subject to agreed on-call and maintenance practices)
   - Latency: target p95 <= 90ms for dedicated pool. If tolerable quality regression testing and additional validation are performed, we can move to p95 <= 80ms (to be agreed at pilot close)
   - Emergency maintenance rollback: Redwood commits to rollback within 60 minutes for incidents that impact the dedicated pool (subject to reasonable coordination)

3) Commercials & next steps
   - Price: we'll forward a dedicated-capacity pricing delta and a proposed credit schedule (Marissa to provide details).
   - DocuSign: when you'll be ready, we'll send an updated SLA via DocuSign (placeholder link shared below).

Attached: updated SLA draft (minor edits), cost-impact-estimate.xlsx (initial numbers), runbook-stub.txt (ops playbook).

Proposed next steps: quick sync early next week to confirm QPS by model and pilot acceptance criteria. Once you confirm, we'll issue DocuSign envelope and kick off provisioning (T+5 business days typical).

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4582

Best,
Karthik
